items.title: Dave Frishberg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001
items.q: my favorite gig was with Becky Kilgore... we had a job together in a hotel two nights a week for five years. And just a duo.

ctx.x: They were a great match, weren’t they? © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-

Yeah. Oh yeah. And then in L.A., oh I don’t know I guess the most fun I had was the Herb Alpert days. In Portland I think my favorite gig was with Becky Kilgore, the singer, the Portland singer who I met up there and we had a job together in a hotel two nights a week for five years. And just a duo. And I loved that gig. And last week I finished three weeks at the Algonquin in New York in what I described to myself as the favorite gig of my life it was so much fun. So that was — I just finished a memorable gig.
Who was on that gig, was it just you?

items.title: Rebecca Kilgore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997
items.q: I’ve been extremely lucky in my relationship with Dave Frishberg... he got me on the Arbors label... I just recorded another thing for Arbors with Dave Frishberg... he and I do a few duets

ctx.x: Do you do y our own promotion and all that?

Pretty much but I’m not very good at it. It’s very hard if you’re insecure to kind of try to sell yourself. So I just try to work on the music and hope that things sell themselves. And I’ve been extremely lucky in my relationship with Dave Frishberg, he was an Arbors recording artist and he got me on the Arbors label and then I got to know Dan Barrett and Dan Barrett I think was instrumental in getting me on my first jazz party which was the Triangle Jazz Party in Tennessee. And then from that, you know this, and…

“Hi you don’t know me but I sing pretty good.” Yeah that’s tough. Click. Speaking of Arbors, I want to get this on tape here, from Jazz Times talking about your album with Dave, and this particular fellow says, “Kilgore sings with a happy voice filled of erudition and charm, turning every number into a sweet explication of the American song.”
